description:
Mi nombre es Bautista Legno, Me gradué como Técnico en Programación en el IPET N° 59 "25 de Mayo", etapa en la que también amplié mi base técnica completando diversos cursos Full Stack.

Actualmente estudio Ingeniería Agronómica en la Facultad de Ciencias Agrarias (UNR). Mis intereses se centran en crear un puente directo entre la tecnología y el campo; busco aplicar el pensamiento lógico y las herramientas de software para diseñar soluciones innovadoras que optimicen los procesos agrícolas.
summary: Space Up Analytics is an interactive platform developed in Python for Jupyter/Google Colab environments. It combines historical satellite telemetry, stochastic precipitation modeling, and agronomic decision rules to assist with planting planning and the technical auditing of agricultural plots (with an initial focus on Argentina’s "Core Zone").
details:
Space Up Analytics is an agronomic satellite intelligence platform designed to evaluate planting viability and analyze the historical performance of agricultural plots. The system works by connecting in real time to the NASA POWER and MODIS APIs to extract data on precipitation, soil temperature, surface moisture, and green indices (NDVI). Through an interactive map, it processes the exact coordinates of a field and cross-references meteorological variables with the specific bioclimatic requirements of each crop to issue automatic diagnoses.

The entire development is built within the Google Colab environment, using Python as the primary language. The architecture integrates libraries such as Pandas and NumPy for handling time series and stochastic simulations, ipywidgets and Plotly for the interactive interface and dynamic visualization, and ipyleaflet along with Geopy for cartography and geolocation. Queries to the satellite servers are managed via HTTP requests structured with the requests library.

The project's creativity lies in the interdisciplinary synergy between data science and agronomic engineering, reflecting the team's structure where Thiago Osellame's computational development integrates with Bautista Legno's agronomic design. The algorithm does not merely display a statistical dashboard; it transforms raw data into active, real-time decision-making. It uses conditional probability chains to simulate future rainfall scenarios and model soil drying rates based on the month, allowing the code to dictate concrete operational actions. To ensure uninterrupted performance, the team programmed a backup stochastic climate simulator that activates automatically if the NASA servers experience downtime, ensuring that field evaluations never stop.

This technological precision offers the benefit of replacing empirical intuition with 15-day projections, indicating the exact moment when the field conditions will be suitable for machinery traffic and reach the optimal temperature for germination. Furthermore, it automates genetic selection by recommending short, intermediate, or long cycles depending on the projected percentage of available water, and it executes a forensic analysis that calculates the carbon balance and nutrient extraction (N-P-K) based on the last five years of crop rotation. The anticipated impact of this tool is the comprehensive optimization of regional yields, ensuring that the production strategy accurately responds to the actual environmental supply in order to maximize profitability while protecting long-term sustainability and soil structure.
